item_argument_dependencies.argument: Define the exact finite-channel semigroup law and intermediate-channel factorization used for CP-divisibility; make no continuity or universal Markovianity claim.

Define finite jump labels, ordered times, branch operators, unnormalized branch states, repeated componentwise Riemann branch weights, and physical time units; normalization is proved by the consuming theorem.

Adopt finite system and environment spaces, a fixed product preparation independent of the system input, a declared joint unitary family, its finite partial-trace reduction, and a separately selected time-homogeneous GKSL approximation.

Diagonalize the finite environment state, derive Kraus operators from partial-trace coordinates, use the published basis-independence characterization to change environment basis, prove adjoint-square normalization by joint unitarity, then give a finite dephasing model violating the semigroup law and CP-divisibility.

Compute the four matrix-unit actions of the qubit GKSL generator, sum their finite-dimensional operator-exponential series directly with the real/complex exponential convention stated, and use the finite GKSL theorem for channel validity.

Split the bounded finite generator into no-jump and jump superoperators, prove no-jump contraction, derive variation of constants entrywise, iterate with a factorial remainder bound and monomial simplex volumes, identify ordered terms with trajectory branches, and normalize using trace preservation.
Compute the conditional two-qubit rotations, choose exact zero and revival times from the unit circle, and show equal intermediate states become distinct later outputs.

Evaluate the no-jump and one-jump branches from the amplitude-damping model, use ensemble normalization to derive each finite-horizon jump mass, and use exponential decay to normalize the law on the half-line.
